title: Color, class and Creole clubs
summary: Whether Jelly was prejudiced against darker people; Creole class and caste, the Autocrats Club, and his regard for King Oliver.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Some people talk about your brother as if you didn't like dark people. I don't know, but as far as I knew... Oh no, he wasn't pregnant. I don't think he was really prejudiced. He might have kidded somebody sometime, you know. But some people talk like he... He wasn't pregnant at all, but I'm going to tell you,
in Louisiana a long time ago, people believed in class and caste, you know. I guess, yeah, that's right. They say some of the late CREOs, you know, didn't want to...
Right now, downtown, there, that Autocrats Club,
they're losing members by the school because they've got too many dark people in there. Really? Is that way?

Right down on St. Menard Avenue, that's Autocrats Club. Yeah. And at one time, there was nothing... You'd go back there, you really thought it was... They had the Iroquois Club here, that if you weren't Creole by birth, you couldn't belong to it.
I know there was the Franz of Meek in the old days. Oh yeah, my sister went to the Franz of Meek and I didn't.
That's why I'm looking at what they threw in rice on them.

They had a beautiful wedding. And I mean, they made it... It'd be 20 years in September, 20 years in July since I've seen my sister to live around her. I've just been up there for a short visit and things like that.
I was wondering if your brother did ever make any remarks about the darker people in Chicago or anything. Well, I wouldn't...

Because he was crazy about King Oliver. Yeah, that's right. And he was a great big black man. He played with a lot of those dark people. That's right. He's my son, he's the best man, talking about his last single minutes of... But he took communion and he... He's a free man. Last... Last... Two minutes of being a bachelorhood. I told him, boy, you better hurry up out of here. Because he looked like he was going to be late for his own wedding. That's her sister that lives in New York. Oh, yes. Here she comes down the steps. That's pretty cool, right? But they had nine children, mind you. I mean, they have beautiful front steps now and a porch and everything. But they didn't have anything but this here. I mean, a man making a post office salary with nine children, he couldn't expect to have too much. No, no. They got things better now, I guess.
Now she has central air conditioning, heating, everything. But she works every day right along with my son. She's secretary at the school.
